title: Your December pension tax refund may be automatic — a new family deduction may not be
summary: FACT: Sa December 2026 pension payment, Japan Pension Service will automatically recalculate 2026 withholding using the higher basic deduction and generally refund overwithheld tax. Pero kung may spouse o dependent na newly qualifies only because the income limit rose from ¥580,000 to ¥620,000, JPS says you generally need a 2026 tax return to claim that deduction.
why_it_matters: Two parts of the same tax reform work differently. The basic-deduction correction is built into December pension withholding, but a newly eligible spouse/dependent can still require a tax return—so assuming JPS will fix everything automatically can leave a legitimate deduction unclaimed.

claims.text: The 2026 tax reform was enacted through the Act Partially Amending the Income Tax Act, etc. (Act No. 12 of 2026) and raised the basic deduction and family-income eligibility thresholds.
claims.basis: Japan Pension Service identifies the enacted law and pension-related changes.

claims.text: For 2026 pension income tax, JPS uses the pre-reform basic deduction through the November pension payment, then recalculates the full-year tax using the revised deduction at the December 2026 payment.
claims.basis: JPS and the independent Life Insurance Culture Center both describe the December reconciliation.

claims.text: If the December reconciliation produces an overpayment, JPS says the amount is generally refunded.
The reform raises the total-income threshold for ordinary spouse/dependent eligibility from ¥580,000 to ¥620,000 for 2026 income tax.
claims.basis: JPS table explicitly shows ¥620,000 with ¥580,000 as the pre-reform threshold.

claims.text: For a relative who newly qualifies in 2026 because of the revised income requirement, JPS says a final income-tax return is generally required to claim the deduction.
claims.basis: JPS states this directly and the Life Insurance Culture Center independently highlights the same filing case.

claims.text: The 2026 pension dependent declaration was already being mailed from September 10, 2025, and current JPS instructions distinguish that form's ¥580,000 threshold from the ¥620,000 threshold used under the revised rule going forward.
claims.basis: Current JPS form instructions and mailing history.

claims.text: Current JPS instructions distinguish 2026 from later pension withholding: the 2026 age-65+ threshold remains ¥2.05 million and the under-65 threshold ¥1.55 million; ¥2.14 million and ¥1.64 million apply from 2027.
claims.basis: Current JPS instructions explicitly label the thresholds by tax year.

claims.text: The practical trap is administrative: the same reform contains an automatic December correction for the pensioner's own basic deduction but a non-automatic route for some newly eligible family deductions.
claims.basis: The conclusion follows from the different official transition procedures.

content.policy_status: ENACTED. The 2026 income-tax changes are law. The special pension withholding reconciliation is scheduled for the December 2026 pension payment; the raised ¥620,000 family-income threshold applies to 2026 income tax even though the already-issued 2026 pension declaration used the old ¥580,000 threshold.
content.key_message: Dalawang magkaibang process: December can automatically fix overwithholding from the higher basic deduction, but it may not add a spouse/dependent who only became eligible under the new ¥620,000 income limit.
content.who_is_affected: Most relevant to old-age pension recipients who have income tax withheld and to pensioners whose spouse or other qualifying dependent has 2026 total income above ¥580,000 but no more than ¥620,000. Other eligibility conditions still apply.
content.when: The automatic pension-tax reconciliation happens at the December 2026 pension payment. Any needed final/refund return is handled after the 2026 tax year under the normal tax-return process.
content.financial_impact: The automatic refund varies with pension amount, deductions and tax already withheld. For an ordinary qualifying spouse/dependent, JPS shows a ¥380,000 deduction from taxable income; that is not a ¥380,000 cash refund, and the actual tax saving depends on taxable income and tax rate.
content.risk_if_ignored: MED: the pensioner's own basic-deduction overpayment should generally be reconciled automatically, but an eligible family deduction can be missed if the household assumes the December adjustment covers it too.
content.deadline: No special September deadline. Check the December pension payment and the 2026 pension withholding certificate, then use the normal 2026 final/refund-return process if a relative newly qualifies and the deduction was not reflected.
content.potential_benefit: Recover overwithheld tax and avoid leaving a newly available spouse/dependent deduction unclaimed.
content.downside: Not every pensioner needs to file. The ¥620,000 income test is only one eligibility condition among several.
content.common_mistake: Do not assume the new ¥2.14M/¥1.64M withholding thresholds govern ordinary 2026 payments; current JPS guidance assigns them to 2027. Also do not assume the automatic December recalculation automatically adds newly eligible family members.
content.what_to_do_now: If a spouse/dependent is near the old threshold, estimate that person's full-year 2026 total income and keep income records. Do not file early. When the December payment and later withholding certificate arrive, check whether the pension tax was reconciled and whether the family deduction is reflected.
content.what_to_wait_for: Wait for the December 2026 pension reconciliation and the 2026 pension withholding certificate before deciding whether a return is needed. Use the National Tax Agency's official 2026 filing guidance when available.
content.strongest_counterinterpretation: For many pensioners this requires no extra action. JPS is explicitly building the basic-deduction correction into December. The filing issue is concentrated among people who want to claim a deduction that the pre-reform pension declaration could not capture or another refund-producing deduction.
content.what_would_change_mind: ALAM would downgrade the action need if JPS or NTA publishes a mechanism that automatically retrofits newly eligible ¥580k-¥620k dependents into the 2026 pension reconciliation. It would raise urgency if official guidance identifies a special deadline or correction process beyond the ordinary final/refund-return route.

reading_levels.30 sec: FACT: JPS will recalculate 2026 pension withholding in December using the higher basic deduction and generally refund overpaid tax automatically. Fine print: if your spouse/dependent only became eligible because the income limit rose from ¥580k to ¥620k, JPS says you generally need a 2026 tax return to claim that family deduction. PREPARE records now; check December before filing.
reading_levels.2 min: The 2026 pension-tax reform has two tracks. JPS will do a full-year December recalculation for the pensioner's own basic deduction, so overpaid withholding is generally automatic. But the 2026 pension dependent declaration was already sent from September 2025 and used ¥580,000. The new law raised the limit to ¥620,000 for 2026 income tax, so JPS says a newly eligible spouse/dependent generally requires a final tax return. The widely quoted ¥2.14M age-65+ and ¥1.64M under-65 pension withholding thresholds are for 2027, not ordinary 2026 withholding.

outcomes: Understand why one pension tax correction is automatic while another can require filing.
Know what to check before deciding whether to file.
learning.background: JPS withholds income tax from qualifying old-age pension payments. A 2026 law increased the basic deduction and some family-income eligibility limits. Because the 2026 pension declaration process had already begun before the law changed, JPS uses different transition procedures for the two changes.

terms.meaning: Tax withheld before the pension payment reaches the recipient.
terms.why_it_matters: December can correct tax already withheld earlier in 2026.

terms.meaning: The pension declaration used to tell JPS about eligible spouses, dependents and certain deductions.
terms.why_it_matters: The 2026 form was issued before the later law change and used the old threshold.

terms.term: 確定申告 / 還付申告
terms.meaning: A final income-tax return, including a refund return when too much tax was paid.
terms.why_it_matters: JPS says this is generally needed for a relative newly eligible under the revised 2026 family-income test.

how_it_works.title: 1. Old calculation through November
how_it_works.explanation: JPS keeps using the pre-reform basic-deduction calculation through the November 2026 pension payment.

how_it_works.title: 2. December catch-up
how_it_works.explanation: At the December payment, JPS recalculates the full 2026 tax with the revised basic deduction and generally refunds any excess withholding.

how_it_works.title: 3. Newly eligible family members are different
how_it_works.explanation: The old 2026 pension declaration used ¥580,000. If a family member only becomes eligible under the new ¥620,000 limit, JPS says a final return is generally required to claim that deduction.

learning.example: If an otherwise-eligible dependent has 2026 total income of ¥600,000, that is above the old ¥580,000 line but within the new ¥620,000 line. The pensioner's own December basic-deduction adjustment can be automatic, while the dependent deduction may still require a tax return.
takeaways: December 2026 has a built-in pension withholding catch-up.
A newly eligible family member in the ¥580k-¥620k band is not necessarily added automatically.
Keep income records and check December plus the withholding certificate before filing.

action_plan.goal: Let the automatic reconciliation happen while preserving what is needed to claim a family deduction the transition process misses.
action_plan.who_should_act: Pension recipients with tax withheld, especially if a spouse/dependent is expected to have 2026 total income above ¥580,000 but no more than ¥620,000.
action_plan.deadline: No immediate special deadline; review after the December 2026 pension payment.
prepare: Full-year 2026 income records for the family member

steps.action: Check full-year 2026 total income and other eligibility conditions.
steps.how: Use actual income records; do not compare ¥620,000 directly with gross receipts unless the official income calculation says to.
steps.done_when: You know whether the ¥580k-to-¥620k transition is relevant.

steps.action: Review the December pension tax deduction/refund effect.
steps.how: Compare the December payment notice with earlier payments.
steps.done_when: You have confirmed the pension withholding adjustment or identified a discrepancy to verify.

steps.action: Use the 2026 withholding certificate to see whether the spouse/dependent deduction still needs claiming.
steps.how: Compare the certificate and income records with current JPS/NTA guidance.
steps.done_when: You know whether a return is still needed.

steps.action: Use the NTA's official 2026 final/refund-return process after year-end if the deduction applies and was not reflected.
steps.how: Follow official NTA filing guidance when published.
steps.done_when: The return is accepted or official guidance confirms no filing is needed.

mistakes_to_avoid: Assuming December automatically adds every newly eligible family member.
Comparing the ¥620,000 total-income test directly with gross salary or pension receipts.
Assuming income under ¥620,000 alone guarantees eligibility.

decision_rules.if: No family member becomes newly eligible under the revised test and there are no other refund-producing issues
decision_rules.then: Usually let the December reconciliation run; this story alone does not create a reason to file.

decision_rules.if: A family member is newly eligible because 2026 total income is above ¥580,000 but within ¥620,000 and the deduction is not reflected
decision_rules.then: Prepare to claim it through the official 2026 final/refund-return process.

action_plan.follow_up: Re-check JPS and NTA guidance after the December 2026 pension payment and when official 2026 filing guidance is available.

editorial_visual.scene: a pension statement split into two neat lanes: one lane automatically returns a few yen coins in December, while the other lane stops at a family-deduction form waiting to be filed; restrained calendar symbolism, no readable text or logos
editorial_visual.caption: One tax correction is automatic; the other may still need paperwork
